## 🔹 Transition 1: Return to South Africa in 1990

### 🟩 Before (1963–1990)
- Max Sisulu was born in 1945 in Soweto and grew up in a household of anti-apartheid activists (his parents, Walter and Albertina Sisulu).
- In 1963, at age 19, he and his mother were arrested after his father went into hiding. Walter Sisulu was later sentenced to life imprisonment in the Rivonia Trial.
- Following his release, Max left South Africa for exile via Botswana, traveling to Tanzania to join Umkhonto we Sizwe (the ANC’s armed wing).
- Over the next two decades, he lived in exile across Africa and Europe:
  - Studied political economy at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics (Moscow, 1969)
  - Completed a senior military training course in Skhodnya, USSR (1972)
  - Spent a year as ANC representative in Budapest (1985)
  - Worked in Lusaka, Zambia (1986–1990) as head of the ANC’s Department of Economic Planning
- During this time, he developed expertise in economic policy and became a key strategist for the ANC’s economic planning.

> ✅ *Context*: The apartheid regime intensified repression, forcing many ANC leaders into exile. Sisulu’s early years were defined by political persecution and exile, shaping his future role as an economic planner.

---

### 🟨 During (1990–1994)
- In **1990**, Sisulu returned to South Africa as part of the broader negotiations to end apartheid.
- This marked a turning point: the first major democratic opening since the 1960s.
- Upon return, he became the **founding director of the National Institute of Economic Policies (NIEP)** in Johannesburg — an ANC think-tank focused on post-apartheid economic development.
- In **1993**, he completed a Master of Public Administration at Harvard Kennedy School, further strengthening his technical and policy credentials.
- He was elected to the ANC National Executive Committee (NEC) in 1994, and soon after became chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on the Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP), the ANC’s flagship social and economic policy.

> ✅ *Key events*: Return to South Africa, establishment of NIEP, Harvard degree, appointment to NEC and RDP committee.  
> ✅ *Significance*: His return allowed him to transition from exile strategist to a central figure in shaping South Africa’s post-apartheid economic policies.

---

### 🟧 After (1994 onward)
- In **April 1994**, Sisulu was elected to the National Assembly in South Africa’s first democratic elections.
- He played a key role in overseeing the implementation of the RDP, which aimed to address poverty, housing, and infrastructure.
- His leadership in economic policy and parliamentary oversight laid the foundation for his later role as Speaker.
- He remained active in the ANC, re-elected to the NEC and NWC in 2002 and 2007, and continued to serve as chair of the NEC’s Subcommittee on Economic Transformation.

> ✅ *Legacy*: His return in 1990 was not just a personal homecoming — it was the beginning of a new era in South African politics, where economic planning and institutional reform became central. Sisulu’s expertise bridged the gap between revolutionary struggle and democratic governance.

---
